title: Qwen3.6-27B: Flagship-Level Coding in a 27B Dense Model
description: Alibaba's Qwen3.6-27B delivers flagship-level agentic coding performance, surpassing the previous-generation open-source flagship Qwen3.5-397B-A17B across all major coding benchmarks. The model is 55.6GB compared to 807GB, making it much more accessible. Simon tested it with a quantized version showing outstanding results for a local model.
author: Simon Willison

title: Firefox 150 includes 271 vulnerability fixes found by Claude Mythos Preview
description: Mozilla's CTO Bobby Holley shares their experience applying an early version of Claude Mythos Preview to Firefox, resulting in 271 vulnerability fixes in Firefox 150. He notes that 'Defenders finally have a chance to win, decisively' and describes how teams can succeed with focused AI security research.
author: Bobby Holley (via Simon Willison)

title: Changes to GitHub Copilot Individual plans - Agentic workflows changing compute demands
description: GitHub tightened Copilot usage limits, paused individual plan signups, and restricted Claude Opus 4.7 to the Pro+ plan. The announcement notes that 'Agentic workflows have fundamentally changed Copilot's compute demands' with long-running, parallelized sessions consuming far more resources than the original plan structure was designed to support.
author: Simon Willison

title: Is Claude Code going to cost $100/month? Pricing confusion
description: Anthropic quietly updated their pricing page to add a $100/month Claude Code option, then reverted it. Simon analyzes the confusing state of Claude Code pricing and compares it to GitHub Copilot's pricing changes in the evolving landscape of AI coding agents.
author: Simon Willison

title: ChatGPT Images 2.0 released
description: OpenAI released ChatGPT Images 2.0, their latest image generation model. Sam Altman said the leap from gpt-image-1 to gpt-image-2 was equivalent to jumping from GPT-3 to GPT-5. Simon tests it with a 'raccoon with a ham radio' prompt to evaluate the model's capabilities.
author: Simon Willison

title: llm-openrouter 0.6 released with model refresh
description: Simon released llm-openrouter 0.6 with a new `llm openrouter refresh` command for refreshing the list of available models without waiting for cache to expire. He added this feature to try Kimi 2.6 on OpenRouter as soon as it became available.
author: Simon Willison

title: Claude Token Counter upgraded with model comparisons
description: Simon upgraded his Claude Token Counter tool to compare token counts between different models. He found that Claude Opus 4.7's new tokenizer uses 1.46x the number of tokens as Opus 4.6 for the same input, meaning it will be around 40% more expensive despite the same pricing per token.
author: Simon Willison

title: Headless everything for personal AI
description: Matt Webb and Marc Benioff discuss the rise of 'headless' services designed for AI agents rather than human GUI interaction. Salesforce Headless 360 exposes entire platforms as APIs, MCP, and CLI so AI agents can access data directly. This trend could disrupt per-head SaaS pricing schemes.
author: Simon Willison

title: Changes in the system prompt between Claude Opus 4.6 and 4.7
description: Anthropic published their system prompts for Claude chat, enabling analysis of how the system prompt evolves. Simon examines the differences between Opus 4.6 and 4.7 system prompts and created a git timeline tool to browse the changes.
author: Simon Willison

title: PyCon US 2026 in Long Beach with new AI and security tracks
description: PyCon US 2026 is coming May 13-19 in Long Beach, California, featuring new AI and security tracks this year. The conference includes tutorials, sprints, and core conference talks.
author: Simon Willison

title: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B vs Claude Opus 4.7 - Pelican benchmark
description: Simon compared pelican-drawing capabilities between Alibaba's Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.7, finding that the local Qwen model drew a better pelican than Claude Opus 4.7, continuing his 'pelican riding a bicycle' benchmark for testing models.
author: Simon Willison

title: Claude Code and LLM Agents - Practical Coding Experience
description: Andrej Karpathy discusses Claude Code as 'the first convincing demonstration of what an LLM Agent looks like' that lives on your computer. He shares insights from extensive hands-on experience with AI-assisted coding workflows, noting how LLM programming languages may look different from what humans converged on as AI may not share our tradeoffs.
author: Andrej Karpathy
